shape.text: An API key begins fw_ (lowercase, with an underscore). The documentation writes keys as fw_ followed by a truncated body, and provider tooling accepts a key only if it starts with fw_ or fpk_ (case-sensitive). No documented length or alphabet exists.
The body after fw_ is 22 or 24 characters (25 or 27 in all).

unresolved.reason: Based on nine distinct public non-placeholder values observed by the maintainers (six with a 22-character body, three with 24); no provider source states a length and a distribution of nine is a hypothesis, not a measurement.

shape.text: The body uses letters and digits, possibly a base58 alphabet.

unresolved.reason: The observed values avoided 0, O, I and l, which is consistent with base58 but is an inference; no provider source states the alphabet.

issuance.text: Keys are created in the console (API Keys) or with the firectl command, including for service accounts. The create response returns the key once, together with a prefix field described as the first characters, provided to visually identify the key.
No Fireworks AI key was issued or observed for this record.

unresolved.reason: No key was issued for the research; several issued keys would show whether the length varies.

collisions.text: Fire Pass keys begin fpk_, share the FIREWORKS_API_KEY variable and are a separate live prefix.

unresolved.reason: The prefix is documented, but its body length and alphabet were not found.
Only older documentation and a third-party scanning-tool documentation page mention an unprefixed form; no source confirms an older shape.

collisions.text: The key id (keyId), the prefix display value, account ids, model paths (accounts/fireworks/models/...), service-account emails, identifiers such as fw_id, fw_version and fw_spec, and a keychain reference written by the fireconnect tool are not keys.
